options: What is this user allowed to do?
Who is this user?
Which records can this user see?
Which fields are visible to this user?
questions.explain: Authentication proves identity — who the user is. Authorization, a separate step, decides what they're then allowed to do.

questions.q: A user logs in through SSO instead of a username and password. What happens to their Salesforce authorization rules for that session?
options: They are relaxed, since SSO is considered a trusted login method
They stay exactly the same — authorization is independent of the authentication method used
They are tightened automatically for every SSO login
They no longer apply, since SSO logins bypass profiles and permission sets
questions.explain: Authorization (profiles, permission sets, sharing rules) is evaluated the same way regardless of how a user authenticated. Changing the login method never changes what the user is authorized to do.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of 'something you have' as an authentication factor?
options: A password
A fingerprint
A mobile device running an authenticator app
A security question answer
questions.explain: A possessed device, like a phone running Salesforce Authenticator, is the 'something you have' factor. Passwords and security question answers are 'something you know'; a fingerprint is 'something you are'.

questions.q: Since when has Salesforce required MFA for direct UI logins to the platform?
options: February 2022
It has never been required, only recommended
Since Salesforce was founded
Only for Government Cloud orgs
questions.explain: Salesforce began requiring MFA for direct UI logins starting February 2022, making it a mandatory part of the login contract rather than an optional add-on.

questions.q: What is the role of a session security level (Standard vs. High Assurance)?
options: It determines which object permissions a profile grants
It lets an authorization decision depend on how strongly the session was authenticated
It replaces the need for field-level security
It controls which fields appear on a page layout
questions.explain: Session security levels are the bridge between authentication and authorization: they let Salesforce require a stronger login method (like MFA) before permitting a sensitive action.
